feedback:
The proposal is a serious design, not a sketch: all fourteen requirements appear exactly once in the coverage table with substantive engineering behind each, every decision carries alternatives that name real tradeoffs rather than strawmen, and several of the spec's harder demands are met structurally rather than by assertion (RunManifest snapshotting so a mode edit cannot change a running job, tombstone plus generation token in the same transaction as the worker insert so a late response cannot recreate a deleted recording, a delivery_attempts row committed before any event is posted with no automatic retry, and measurement protocols kept explicitly unperformed with no latency or language claim made on documentation alone). It nonetheless has defects that an implementer would have to invent behavior around, so it is not ready.

Confirmed objections, verified against the proposal text. (1) Result identity: data_lifecycle states 'A recording has exactly one source transcript' while D-024 and the History coverage entry allow reprocessing through a different speech model; results rows carry speech_model_id but no parent-result link, so after a second recognition nothing identifies which transcript a translation, rewrite, or meeting note derived from. (2) Recovery: the launch sweep defines outcomes for arming, capturing, delivery attempts, scratch, and staging, but not for a manifest found in finalizing, recognizing, refining, or rewriting, while verification asserts 'the recovery outcomes listed in the data lifecycle' for every stage boundary; separately, 'the audio is finalized by reading what was flushed' for ALAC in CAF after SIGKILL is asserted with no basis and is not even listed as an open question. (3) Ingest contract: D-018 emits canonical buffers plus a live/seekable descriptor with no presentation time, clock domain, or discontinuity marker, while D-023 requires two streams aligned by host time; and the long-input ceiling test bounds 'peak resident size' of the app when recognition runs in a helper process (D-003), so it does not measure the process that could accumulate. (4) Delivery: D-009 states that success cannot be confirmed on the paste and typing paths, while failure_behavior specifies 'Paste rejected by the target: fall through to synthesized Unicode keystrokes' without naming the signal that detects rejection; and 'accessibility set-value on the latched element' is never distinguished from selected-text insertion, so as written the first rung can replace a field's entire contents. The 300 ms restore delay is a bare constant with no basis or reconsideration condition. (5) Permission revocation: 'the session moves to failed(capturing, permissionRevoked)' is written once for the whole permission list, so losing Accessibility or browser Automation during recognition would terminate a recording that is still valid. (6) Shortcuts: toggle-on-keyDown and push-to-talk arming after a 200 ms hold are not separated into distinct bindings and the first 200 ms is undefined; the watchdog that 'finalizes at the configured maximum hold' is a recording-duration cap, which the spec prohibits, even though its intent is stuck-key recovery. (7) Model activation: the staged rename and the manifest pointer update span the filesystem and SQLite with no ordering or crash rule, renaming over a populated live directory is not the atomic operation described, and a pinned in-flight run needs the previous weights to survive activation. (8) Retention: architecture says RecordingStore enforces tombstone and job-token rules for every writer, but the age, size, and drop-audio-keep-text policies are never stated to take leases, and removing audio under an admitted job or active playback has no transition. (9) Phased plan: the spec makes a complete phased implementation plan part of the deliverable, and phases 1 through 9 are a feature ordering with no entry conditions, exit evidence, schema migration work, or rollback; only phase 0 has an exit criterion, software gain and media pause appear in no phase, and D-020, D-004, and D-027 settle runtime, preemption, and residency before the phase 2 bake-off that could invalidate them. (10) Validator scope: the fail-closed path exists (retry once, then the normalized transcript, marked as a fallback), but the checks are English-shaped (interrogative survival, content-word recall) while D-017 promises multilingual recognition, and free-form custom prompts have no stated mapping onto a declared transformation set, so the mode-plus-language pairs with no usable validator need a defined behavior.

Objections I judged overstated. D-108's claim that chunk-boundary preemption may be impossible is not supported: windowed whisper decoding and token-level generation both stop cleanly at those points; the fair residue is that resume fidelity, cancellation latency, and helper RSS belong in the bake-off, and the 8 GB budget is already recorded as declared-size arithmetic with a reconsider condition. D-109 is right that a media-key toggle plus a device-idle flag is weaker than ownership, but the proposal records this as an assumption with basis and reconsideration; the proportionate fix is to rename the claim and default resume off, not to delete the feature. D-106 understates what the design already does (below-threshold segments are unattributed, names live in a separate mapping); the residue worth fixing is echo and cross-channel leakage, and the unjustified step of keeping edited names 'where cluster ids are stable' when cluster numbering is arbitrary across runs. D-105's stronger form, that the requirement can be enforced absolutely, asks for more than any design can give; the proposal already calls delimiter framing defense in depth and backs it with an injection corpus. D-201 and D-202 are improvements, not blockers. The review's authority point on the verification gate is fair and cheap to fix: name the normative approver for the behavior tables rather than 'someone who did not write it'.

Not stuck: every confirmed defect is resolvable inside the design as written (a parent link in the result graph, a state-indexed recovery table, a timestamped frame type on the ingest port, an insertion-semantics rung with an observable signal or a hold, a permission-by-state table, a shortcut event table without a mandatory cap, an activation protocol over immutable content-addressed installs, retention under the same lease protocol, and a per-phase gate plan). The three self-declared blocking experiments each already have a stated fallback (whisper.cpp as the reference adapter, symbol scan plus a network-denied session test with an honestly narrowed offline claim, channel-only meetings), so they do not prevent the design from being completed; they need to be sequenced ahead of the boundaries they can invalidate, and the crash-safe audio question needs to join them.

Check mapping: requirements is false because Recording controls carries a duration cap the spec forbids and History cannot express re-recognition provenance; architecture is false for the ingest port contract and the unmeasured helper-side memory boundary; alternatives is true, as each decision weighs options that were genuinely available with costs stated; data_lifecycle is false for result identity, the four undefined recovery states, unverified CAF finalization, activation atomicity, and retention leases; failures is false for the paste-rejection contradiction, the destructive accessibility rung, and the single global revocation rule; maintainability is false because the phase plan lacks gates, evidence, and migration work and orders experiments after the decisions they could overturn; verification is false because the memory test uses one duration and the wrong process scope, the delivery matrix omits destructive replacement, selected-text insertion, delayed paste consumers, and unsnapshotable pasteboards, and the fidelity corpus has no adversarial cases that hold lexical recall while changing meaning; unresolved_decisions is false because insertion semantics, the revocation matrix, the shortcut event table, activation recovery, and the retention lease rule are left for whichever implementation task hits them first.
